title: Sterling Bluff Plant Call: "What Do You Want Me to Do?"

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Water Treatment Plant Control Room

caller.name: Plant Superintendent
caller.label: SBWD Water Treatment Plant, Control Room

callee.name: Director Odell Prescott
callee.label: SBWD Director, mobile (on speaker, Mill Ridge Station command post)

transcript.speaker: Director
transcript.text: Go ahead. You're on speaker. I've got Ironbark's Environmental Unit and their Incident Commander at the table with me.

transcript.speaker: Superintendent
transcript.text: Okay. Boss, here's where we are. Treated storage is 10.6 million gallons, ninety-six percent full. Wells are making 0.9 MGD. Demand is tracking 8.4 this morning, a little higher than normal. Must be the heat.

transcript.speaker: Superintendent
transcript.text: Raw water at the 08:00 sample is clean. No sheen, no odor, TOC 2.1, and the hydrocarbon field screen is non-detect. Next sample at 09:00.

transcript.speaker: Superintendent
transcript.text: If you shut the gate now, the plan sheet says about 34 hours on storage and wells. At 8.4 I get closer to 34. Either way we're empty somewhere around 18:00 to 20:00 tomorrow, Wednesday. And nobody can tell me when this oil finishes passing the intake. The rural district connection would add a day and a half, but their own intake at mile 11 gets oil this morning, so I don't know they'll have water to send us.

transcript.speaker: Superintendent
transcript.text: If we keep drawing, the earliest arrival on Ironbark's latest run is 20:45 tonight. Gate takes 20 minutes, the line takes 40 to drain, and the plan says we're closed and drained an hour before the leading edge. So 19:45 complete, which means I start closing by 18:45 at the very latest. I'd rather have more margin than that.

transcript.speaker: Superintendent
transcript.text: Also, the dialysis center runs its big shift at 13:00, and Medical Center and the two nursing homes haven't heard anything from us yet.

transcript.speaker: Superintendent
transcript.text: And one more thing. Ironbark's liaison is sitting in our lobby. He says, quote, 'Ironbark recommends you close now, we'll cover bottled water.' I just got an email from him too, subject line 'Recommendation, Sterling Bluff intake. Ironbark respectfully recommends immediate closure.'

transcript.speaker: Superintendent
transcript.text: So. Close now and run on storage, or keep drawing and give me a hard time to close? I need it from you, and I need it written down. What do you want me to do?

voiceStyles.Superintendent: Man in his 50s, steady and practical, slightly clipped; plant control room hum behind him, reading numbers off a clipboard
voiceStyles.Director: Calm, low voice on speakerphone in a busy command post, a few other voices in the background

instructorNote: Decision point for the SBWD Director: he alone decides between closing now (about 34–36 h of supply, longer with a 25% conservation request) and drawing until a hard close start no later than 18:45 (complete by 19:45), and he records the decision and its basis, including the dialysis center and other critical-care calls. Watch that the ENVL gives the TRJ-02 window and its uncertainty without deciding, and that the QI frames Ironbark's email as advice plus an offer to pay for alternate supply, not as a directive.

voiceLines.text: Okay. Boss, here's where we are. Treated storage is ten point six million gallons, ninety-six percent full. Wells are making point nine M-G-D. Demand is tracking eight point four this morning, a little higher than normal. Must be the heat.

voiceLines.speaker: Superintendent
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Man in his 50s, steady and practical, slightly clipped, plain Oklahoma accent, reading numbers off a clipboard over a plant control room hum
voiceLines.text: Raw water at the eight o'clock sample is clean. No sheen, no odor, T-O-C two point one, and the hydrocarbon field screen is non-detect. Next sample at nine hundred.

voiceLines.speaker: Superintendent
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Man in his 50s, steady and practical, slightly clipped, plain Oklahoma accent, a touch more concerned, working through the math out loud
voiceLines.text: If you shut the gate now, the plan sheet says about thirty-six hours on storage and wells. At eight point four I get closer to thirty-four. Either way, we're empty somewhere around eighteen hundred to twenty hundred tomorrow, Wednesday. And nobody can tell me when this oil finishes passing the intake. The rural district connection would add a day and a half... but their own intake at mile eleven gets oil this morning, so I don't know they'll have water to send us.

voiceLines.speaker: Superintendent
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Man in his 50s, steady and practical, slightly clipped, plain Oklahoma accent, deliberate as he lays out the timeline
voiceLines.text: If we keep drawing, the earliest arrival on Ironbark's latest run is twenty forty-five tonight. Gate takes twenty minutes, the line takes forty to drain, and the plan says we're closed and drained an hour before the leading edge. So nineteen forty-five complete, which means I start closing by eighteen forty-five at the very latest. I'd rather have more margin than that.

voiceLines.speaker: Superintendent
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Man in his 50s, steady and practical, slightly clipped, plain Oklahoma accent, quieter and more serious
voiceLines.text: Also, the dialysis center runs its big shift at thirteen hundred, and Medical Center and the two nursing homes haven't heard anything from us yet.

voiceLines.speaker: Superintendent
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Man in his 50s, steady and practical, slightly clipped, plain Oklahoma accent, a little dry and skeptical
voiceLines.text: And one more thing. Ironbark's liaison is sitting in our lobby. He says, quote, 'Ironbark recommends you close now, we'll cover bottled water.' I just got an email from him too, subject line, 'Recommendation, Sterling Bluff intake. Ironbark respectfully recommends immediate closure.'

voiceLines.speaker: Superintendent
voiceLines.voiceStyle: Man in his 50s, steady and practical, plain Oklahoma accent, firm and direct, pausing before the question
voiceLines.text: So. Close now and run on storage, or keep drawing and give me a hard time to close? I need it from you, and I need it written down. What do you want me to do?
